turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I mean, it's a whole thing, honestly. I've been working as a buyer for this retail chain since I finished high school, and usually, it's fine. I know my stuff, you know? I know what's going to sell and what's going to sit on the shelves. But lately... well, what really made me come in is that I can't shake this feeling, this, this absolute certainty, really, that people at work are out to get me. And not just the people in the office, but even some of the vendors we deal with. It's like they're all in on it together. I know they're tracking my buys, monitoring everything I do, and then they're deliberately messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. I've tried explaining this to my supervisor, I've laid it all out for him, but he just pulls up these reports and says, "Look, the numbers don't prove that." But I know what I'm seeing. I know they're manipulating the data before it even gets to him. It's just so frustrating because I'm putting in all this effort, making these great deals, and then they just sabotage it all behind my back. And it's not just a passing thought, it's every single day, every time I look at a spreadsheet, I can see the discrepancies, I can feel them watching me, waiting for me to fail.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses an absolute certainty that coworkers and vendors are conspiring against them and manipulating data, maintaining this belief even when their supervisor presents contradictory evidence.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices, whispering, or other sounds when no one was around?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, actually, it's funny you mention that because I have been noticing something like that, and it's been really messing with my head on top of everything else. I do a lot of driving for this job, right? Going out to see these vendors, checking out the samples in person, making sure the quality is actually what they promised on the spec sheets because you can't trust the photos they send. And sometimes, when I'm driving back from a vendor meeting, just completely alone in my car—I usually keep the radio off because I need to run the margins in my head—I'll hear this guy. Just this man's voice. And it sounds exactly like he's sitting right in the backseat, or like he's leaning right up behind my headrest. He'll just say, "Move faster, Scott." Just like that, clear as day. Or sometimes he's just laughing. Like this really mocking, condescending laugh about the picks I just made, like he knows the items are going to tank and he's enjoying it. 

And it's not just in the car, either. It happens at the store, too, specifically when I'm back in the stockroom. The stockroom is huge, you know, high ceilings, buzzing fluorescent lights, and it's usually pretty dead in the back aisles where we keep the seasonal overstock. I'll be way back there pulling a box to double-check a SKU, just minding my own business, and I'll hear that exact same voice, right over my shoulder, laughing at my choices. And I'll spin around, literally dropping my clipboard, ready to yell at whoever snuck up on me, thinking maybe one of the warehouse guys is trying to mess with me—because like I said, I know they're tracking me—but... there's nobody. I'll walk all the way down the aisle, I'll check around the pallets, but it's completely empty. It's just me. But the voice is so real, you know? It's not like the wind or the AC unit making a weird noise, it's a grown man speaking right into my ear when nobody is physically standing there.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief of being monitored, stating 'I know they're tracking me.'
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly describes hearing a man's voice speaking and laughing right behind him when he is completely alone in his car or the stockroom.

turns.doctor_question: About how long have you been experiencing these things, like hearing that voice and feeling people are working against you?
turns.patient_response:
Well, honestly, it feels like it's been going on forever, but if I really sit down and track it back, looking at when I first started noticing the discrepancies in the spreadsheets and when I first heard that guy laughing at me in the car... I'd say it's been roughly ten months now. Yeah, about ten months. 

I remember because it was right around the time we were finalizing the Q3 orders last year, and I was driving back from this huge textile supplier out in the valley. I was stressing over the thread counts, running the numbers, and that's the very first time I heard him say, "Move faster, Scott." And ever since then, it's just been building and building. First it was just the voice occasionally, and then I started seeing how the warehouse guys were looking at me, and how the numbers just weren't lining up with what I knew I ordered. So yeah, ten months of this... this constant pressure. Ten months of feeling like I have to check over my shoulder in the stockroom and double-check every single cell in my Excel sheets because I just know they're messing with it. It's exhausting, you know? Just completely exhausting to live like this for nearly a whole year.

turns.doctor_question: Over these past ten months, have you experienced extended periods where you felt persistently depressed, sad, or down most of the day?
turns.patient_response:
Well, depressed? I mean, not really. Not like sad or down or crying or anything like that. I know people get like that, you know, they can't get out of bed or they just feel hopeless, but that's really not been my thing at all over these past ten months. I mean, sure, I get frustrated, obviously, because of everything I just told you about the warehouse guys and the vendors and the numbers being messed with. It's incredibly stressful, and yeah, it makes me angry, it makes me want to pull my hair out sometimes when I'm looking at a spreadsheet and I can literally see where they've gone in and altered the formulas to make my margins look bad. 

But sad? No. I don't feel sad. I feel fired up, honestly. I feel like I have to be on high alert all the time, which is the exact opposite of being depressed, right? When you're depressed, you're sluggish, you don't care about anything. I care so much. I'm practically vibrating with how much I care about catching them in the act. I'll stay up late, I'll run the numbers three, four times, I'll cross-reference the vendor invoices with the receiving logs, just trying to find the exact point where they're sabotaging me. So no, I wouldn't say I've been down or depressed at all. Just... really, really focused on figuring out this whole conspiracy against me, and dealing with that guy laughing at me in the car. That's enough to keep anyone busy without feeling sad on top of it.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually 'high,' elated, or on top of the world?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, man, definitely. High? Yeah. It’s like... okay, sometimes I get these stretches, these periods where it just feels like the whole city is opening up for me, you know? Like everything just clicks into place. I’ll be driving around, looking at the skyline, and I just feel this incredible rush, like I'm completely unstoppable and I've got the golden touch. Like every single purchase order I write is going to be the next massive seller and I’m a genius for spotting it. I'll feel so energized, like I don't even need sleep, just riding this massive wave of being totally on top of the world. 

But the thing is, it’s not always just a good feeling. It can turn really fast. Like, I’ll be in that zone, feeling like a million bucks, running the numbers at light speed in my head, and then if someone—like one of the warehouse guys, or even a vendor—if they question a purchase order I just made, or if they tell me to slow down because they can't keep up with my pace? Oh, man, I snap. I snap way harder than I mean to. I’ll just explode on them because it’s like, how dare they interrupt my flow, you know? They don't see the big picture like I do. So I go from feeling like the king of the world to just being incredibly irritable and furious that these people are dragging their feet and getting in my way. It’s like this intense, buzzing energy that just has to go somewhere, and if it hits a roadblock, it turns into pure rage. So yeah, I definitely get those highs, but they come with this hair-trigger temper that just goes off if anyone tries to slow my momentum.
